items.title: More electricity will make F1 more fun – the new words ahead of the premiere
items.summary: Smaller, lighter and more agile cars. A small revolution in terms of the engines and new concepts for the audience to learn - like active aero. And a brand new stable: Cadillac. The news in Formula 1 is many and the hopes for more exciting racing are high. Here's everything you need to know ahead of the premiere.
items.title_original: Mer el ska göra F1 roligare – nya orden inför premiären
items.summary_original: Mindre, lättare och smidigare bilar. En liten revolution vad gäller motorerna och nya begrepp för publiken att lära sig – som active aero. Och ett helt nytt stall: Cadillac. Nyheterna i formel 1 är många och förhoppningarna på mer spännande racing är stora. Här är allt du behöver veta inför premiären.

items.title: Earth's surface charged, sure - that's when it gets crazy
items.summary: "Grounding" is said to give humans a beneficial electrical balance. The proponents are correct that the Earth's surface has a very weak negative electrical charge. That's when it gets crazy.
items.title_original: Jordens yta laddad, visst – det är sen det blir galet
items.summary_original: ”Jordning” påstås ge människan en välgörande elektrisk balans. Före­språkarna har rätt i att jordens yta har en mycket svag negativ elektrisk laddning. Det är sedan det blir galet.

items.title: The target was missed – the deadly intersections remain
items.summary: The Swedish Transport Administration's goal to remedy 150 of the most dangerous unprotected level crossings by 2025 has not been achieved. On average, five people a year are killed at such crossings, despite major efforts.
items.title_original: Målet missades – de dödliga korsningarna är kvar
items.summary_original: Trafikverkets mål att åtgärda 150 av de allra farligaste oskyddade plankorsningarna senast 2025 har inte uppnåtts. I snitt dödas fem personer om året i sådana korsningar, trots stora satsningar.

items.title: Increased protection for the civilian population in the Baltic Sea and Nordic region
items.summary: Sweden has signed a memorandum of understanding on protecting the civilian population of the Baltic Sea region and the Nordic countries, together with Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway and Poland. This enables the temporary movement of people across borders in the event of crisis or, in the worst-case scenario, war.

items.title: New recommendations for the public's readiness to pay
items.summary: The prevailing global situation and Sweden's high degree of digitization can lead to vulnerabilities in the payment system. It is therefore important that the public ensure that they have different ways to pay, such as cash, payment cards and access to payment services via mobile phone.
items.summary_original: Det rådande omvärldsläget och Sveriges höga grad av digitalisering kan medföra sårbarheter i betalningssystemet. Det är därför viktigt att allmänheten ser till att ha olika sätt att betala på, så som kontanter, betalkort och tillgång till betaltjänster via mobiltelefon.

items.title: Sweden becomes member of Global Coalition on Telecommunications
items.summary: Sweden has become a member of the Global Coalition on Telecommunications (GCOT). It is a global coalition of countries that jointly drive policy development in telecommunications. In connection to Sweden joining the coalition, the members of GCOT launched Security and Resilience Principles for 6G, which Sweden endorses.

items.title: Sweden’s AI Strategy in five minutes
items.summary: Sweden’s AI Strategy sets the long-term direction of the Government’s work with AI. It also provides guidance for work with AI throughout Sweden. The Government adopted the Strategy in February 2026.

items.title: Sweden’s first comprehensive AI strategy aims for top-10 ranking
items.summary: Sweden aims to take a leading role in artificial intelligence. The Government is now presenting a new AI strategy with the aim of providing more effective government agencies, clearer rules for businesses and better conditions for research. The objective is for Sweden to be among the world’s top 10 countries in the field of AI.

items.title: Joint Statement of the Leaders of Ukraine and the Nordic Baltic States (NB8) to mark four years of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine 24 February 2026
items.summary: Gathered in Kyiv – President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the leaders of the Nordic Baltic States (NB8) – Prime Minister of Estonia Kristen Michal, Prime Minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen, President of Finland Alexander Stubb, Prime Minister of Iceland Kristrún Frostadóttir, Prime Minister of Latvia Evika Siliņa, President of Lithuania Gitanas Nausėda, Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre and Prime Minister of Sweden Ulf Kristersson – mark four years since Russia launched its illegal, unjustified full-scale military invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Egypt visit characterised by impactful meetings and deepened cooperation
items.summary: For several intensive February days in Cairo, Minister for Health Care Elisabet Lann met with organisers and actors that care for severely injured patients from Gaza on a daily basis. The trip provided a deeper understanding of the extensive work being done and how Swedish initiatives are contributing.
